questions.prompt: What is a group of stars, gas, and dust called?
questions.explanation: A galaxy is a massive system consisting of stars, stellar remnants, interstellar gas, and dust.

questions.prompt: What do we call a star that explodes?
questions.explanation: A supernova is a powerful and luminous stellar explosion that occurs during the last evolutionary stages of a massive star.

questions.prompt: What is the name of our galaxy?
questions.explanation: Our solar system resides within the Milky Way galaxy.

questions.prompt: What is a shooting star?
questions.explanation: A meteor is a streak of light caused by a space rock burning up as it enters Earth's atmosphere.

questions.prompt: What is a frozen ball of ice and dust called?
questions.explanation: Comets are cosmic snowballs of frozen gases, rock, and dust that orbit the Sun.

questions.explanation: Sputnik 1 was the first artificial Earth satellite, launched by the Soviet Union in 1957.

questions.prompt: What do we call a spacecraft that goes to study space?
questions.explanation: Artificial satellites and robotic probes are sent into space to monitor and study celestial bodies.

questions.prompt: What do we call the study of stars, planets, and space?
questions.explanation: Astronomy is the natural science that studies celestial objects and phenomena.

questions.prompt: What is the force that keeps planets and stars in their place?
questions.explanation: Gravity is the fundamental force of attraction that keeps celestial bodies in their respective orbits.

questions.prompt: What do we call a cloud of gas and dust in space?
questions.explanation: A nebula is an interstellar cloud of dust, hydrogen, helium, and other ionized gases.

questions.prompt: What is a star made of hot gases called?
questions.explanation: The Sun is the star at the center of our Solar System, primarily made of burning hydrogen and helium gases.

questions.prompt: What do we call the path a star or planet follows?

questions.prompt: What is a small rock that orbits the Sun called?

questions.prompt: What do we call the collection of all stars, planets, and galaxies?
questions.explanation: The universe is all of space and time and their contents, including planets, stars, galaxies, and all other forms of matter and energy.

questions.prompt: What do we call a bright object that shines in the night sky?
questions.explanation: Stars are luminous spheres of plasma held together by their own gravity that light up the night sky.

questions.prompt: What is a satellite that goes around a planet called?
questions.explanation: A natural satellite, or moon, is an astronomical body that orbits a planet.

questions.prompt: What is a telescope used for?

choices.text: to see distant stars and galaxies

questions.explanation: Telescopes are optical instruments designed to make distant objects appear closer and clearer.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the first human in space?
questions.explanation: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space when he orbited the Earth in 1961.

questions.prompt: What do we call the visible shapes of stars in the sky?
questions.explanation: A constellation is a group of stars that forms an imaginary outline or pattern on the celestial sphere.

questions.prompt: What is a tool used to look at faraway stars?
questions.explanation: Astronomers use telescopes to gather light and observe remote objects in outer space.

questions.prompt: What is a comet made of?
questions.explanation: Comets are characterized by an nucleus composed of frozen gases, dust, and rocky debris.

questions.prompt: What do astronauts wear in space to stay safe?
questions.explanation: A spacesuit provides environmental protection, oxygen, and pressure maintenance for astronauts in the vacuum of space.

questions.prompt: What do we call the light from a star that reaches Earth?
questions.explanation: Starlight is the light emitted by stars beyond our solar system that penetrates Earth's atmosphere.

questions.prompt: What is the Milky Way?
questions.explanation: The Milky Way is the barred spiral galaxy that contains our Solar System.

questions.prompt: What is a black hole?

choices.text: dark place in space that pulls everything in

questions.explanation: A black hole is a region of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing—no particles or light—can escape from it.

questions.prompt: What do we call a star that is very far from earth?
questions.explanation: A star that is located immense distances away from Earth across interstellar space is referred to as a distant star.

questions.prompt: What is the nearest galaxy to the Milky Way?
questions.explanation: The Andromeda Galaxy is the closest large spiral galaxy to our own Milky Way.

questions.prompt: What is the dark space between stars called?
questions.explanation: Cosmic voids are vast spaces between filaments that contain very few or no galaxies/stars.

questions.prompt: What is a star's life cycle?
questions.explanation: A star undergoes evolutionary phases spanning from formation (birth), main sequence (adulthood), to its eventual collapse or explosion (death).

questions.prompt: What is the Sun mainly made of?
questions.explanation: The Sun is primarily composed of the chemical elements hydrogen and helium in a gaseous plasma state.

questions.prompt: What do we call a space rock that hits Earth?
questions.explanation: A meteorite is a solid piece of debris from an object, such as a comet, asteroid, or meteoroid, that survives its passage through the atmosphere to reach the surface of a planet.

questions.prompt: What is a light-year?

choices.text: the time it takes to rotate
the distance light travels in one year

questions.explanation: A light-year is a unit of astronomical distance equivalent to the distance that light travels in one year.

questions.prompt: What do we call the edge of a black hole?
questions.explanation: The event horizon is the boundary defining the region of space around a black hole from which nothing can escape.

questions.prompt: What do we call a spinning cloud of gas that may form a star?

questions.prompt: What do we call a system with one star and planets orbiting it?
questions.explanation: A solar system comprises a central star bound gravitationally with the planets and bodies that orbit it.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the telescope that looks far into space?
questions.explanation: The Hubble Space Telescope was launched into low Earth orbit to capture high-resolution images of deep space.

questions.prompt: What do we call a very bright flash in the sky caused by a star's explosion?
questions.explanation: A supernova event releases a catastrophic flash of cosmic brightness visible across light-years.

questions.prompt: What is the path that Earth follows around the Sun?
questions.explanation: Earth moves along an elliptical path known as an orbit around the Sun.

questions.prompt: What do we call a group of planets, moons, and the Sun together?

questions.prompt: What do we call the visible group of stars that form shapes?
questions.explanation: Patterns mapped across recognizable clusters of stars are designated as constellations.

questions.prompt: What is a dwarf planet?

questions.prompt: What is the name of the first satellite humans sent into space?
questions.explanation: Sputnik (misspelled as sutnik in options) represents humanity's inaugural artificial step into space exploration.

questions.prompt: What do we call a giant cloud of gas in space?

questions.prompt: What is a celestial body made of ice, dust, and rock that orbits the Sun?

questions.prompt: What do we call a group of billions of stars?
questions.explanation: Galaxies are large systems made up of billions of gravitationally linked stars.

questions.prompt: What do astronauts use to travel to space?

questions.prompt: What is the bright center of a galaxy called?

questions.prompt: What do we call the universe beyond our galaxy?

questions.prompt: What shines in the night sky?

questions.prompt: What do we call the sky at night?

questions.prompt: What is the big bright ball in the sky during the day?

questions.prompt: What is the Moon?

questions.prompt: What is a group of stars called?

questions.prompt: What color are most stars?

questions.prompt: Which shines brighter, Sun or stars?

questions.prompt: What can we see in the sky at night besides stars?

questions.prompt: What is the name of the galaxy we live in?

questions.prompt: What do astronauts wear in space?

questions.prompt: What do rockets do?
questions.explanation: Rockets carry humans, rovers, and tracking modules into orbital locations outside Earth's atmosphere.

questions.prompt: What is a tiny light in the sky called?

questions.prompt: What is a shooting star?

questions.prompt: What shines at night and is big?

questions.prompt: What is a comet?

questions.prompt: What do we call the space where stars are?

questions.prompt: What is a telescope used for?

questions.prompt: What do we call the Sun, Moon, and stars together?

questions.prompt: What is the Moon made of?

questions.prompt: What do we call a bright light in the sky at night?

questions.prompt: What is the Sun?

questions.prompt: What do we call the first man in space?

questions.prompt: What do we see in the sky during daytime?

questions.prompt: What is a bright star in the night sky called?
